tools.name: email_security_check
tools.description: One call answers "is this domain's email properly secured?" — checks MX, SPF, DMARC and mail-gateway/provider detection for ONE domain. The differentiator vs a plain DNS resolver. Use when the user asks about email deliverability, spoofing protection, SPF/DMARC posture, or "is email set up correctly

tools.name: whois_lookup
tools.description: WHOIS / RDAP registration data for ONE domain or IP — registrar, status, creation/expiry, name servers. Returns publicly published WHOIS/RDAP data as-is. Use for "who owns", "when does it expire", "registrar", "when was it registered". One target per call.

tools.name: spf_analyze
tools.description: Analyze a domain's SPF record for ONE domain — the include tree and the RFC 10-DNS-lookup-limit verdict. Use only when the question is specifically about SPF (include tree, lookup count, the `all` qualifier). For an overall "is email secure" grade, use email_security_check instead. One domain per ca

tools.name: dmarc_check
tools.description: Fetch and parse the DMARC policy for ONE domain — presence, p= policy, and the raw record. Use for DMARC-only questions ("does this domain have DMARC", "is it p=reject/quarantine/none"). For full email posture (SPF + DMARC + MX, graded), use email_security_check instead. One domain per call.

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Validate the SYNTAX of an SPF or DMARC record string (no DNS lookup) — returns valid/invalid, a score, a letter grade, and a parsed breakdown. Use when the user pastes an SPF/DMARC record and asks "is this correct?".

tools.name: dkim_discover
tools.description: Discover the DKIM signing keys published for ONE domain. Returns the signing keys found, the mail providers they map to, and their selectors. tools.name: blacklist_check
tools.description: Check whether ONE domain or IP is listed on major email blacklists / RBLs (Spamhaus, Barracuda, SpamCop, SORBS, UCEPROTECT and more). tools.name: search
tools.description: Search DNSai for a domain. Returns result items (id, title, url) covering that domain's DNS records, email-security posture, DMARC policy and WHOIS — pass a result id to fetch for the full data.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch a DNSai result document by id (from search). Runs the lookup and returns the data plus a summary.

tools.name: request_api_key
tools.description: Get a FREE DNSai API key that raises the daily limit from the small shared anonymous allowance to 100 lookups/day. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "request_api_key" references sensitive artifacts (password, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dns_lookup, email_security_check, dmarc_check, blacklist_check, search, request_api_key · Private data: dns_lookup, email_security_check, spf_analyze, dmarc_check, validate, dkim_discover, blacklist_check, search, fetch, request_api_key · Public sink: dns_lookup, email_security_check, spf_analyze, dmarc_check, dkim_discover, blacklist_check, search, request_api_key.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dns_lookup, email_security_check, dmarc_check, blacklist_check, search, request_api_key · Private data: dns_lookup, email_security_check, spf_analyze, dmarc_check, validate, dkim_discover, blacklist_check, search, fetch, request_api_key · Public sink: dns_lookup, email_security_check, spf_analyze, dmarc_check, dkim_discover, blacklist_check, search, request_api_key

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
